The total number of paths of length 2, $T$, is given by summing over all vertices $w$:
$$T = \sum_{w \in V} \binom{d(w)}{2}$$
where $d(w)$ is the degree of vertex $w$.

$T$ counts the total number of pairs $(u, v)$ that share a common neighbor. This count includes pairs that are friends (edges) and pairs that are not friends (non-edges).

For $N=456$, the maximum is achieved by connecting one central vertex to all 455 others. In this configuration, every pair of non-friends (the leaves) shares the central vertex as a common friend. The theoretical upper bound is therefore $K_{max} = \binom{N-1}{2} = \binom{455}{2} = 103,285$. The maximum value is achieved at a very low graph density ($e = N-1$).
